purpose: Atenolol is mainly used to treat high blood pressure and chest pain (angina). It is also used after a heart attack to help protect your heart. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_it_works: Your heart has special receptors that respond to stress hormones like adrenaline, which can make your heart beat faster and harder. Atenolol blocks those receptors, so your heart beats more slowly and with less force. This takes pressure off your heart and lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: You may feel tired or have cold hands and feet, especially when you first start taking it. Some people notice dizziness, slow heartbeat, or mild stomach upset. These effects are often mild and may improve over time.
warnings: Do not stop taking atenolol suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems including chest pain or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, or kidney problems, as atenolol can sometimes mask low blood sugar symptoms and may not be safe for people with certain breathing conditions. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, and be careful when standing up quickly as it can cause dizziness.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 25 to 50 mg taken once a day by mouth. Your doctor may increase this to 100 mg per day if needed. It can be taken with or without food, and it works best if taken at the same time every day.
